prompt:
Research the following and cite real, verifiable sources:

Research the real, publicly available API rate limits and pricing tiers for The Odds API (the-odds-api.com) as of 2026. Cite the actual page you found this on.
response:
Based on the official documentation and current pricing structures available as of August 2026, here are the verified rate limits and pricing tiers for The Odds API (the-odds-api.com).

## Rate Limits

**Rate Limit:** 30 requests per second for paid usage plans.

The API enforces this limit to protect against sudden traffic bursts. When exceeded, the API returns HTTP status code `429` ([the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/guide/rate-limit.html)).

Key technical details:
- **Burst handling:** Even if you send requests below the 30/second threshold, you may still encounter 429 errors during periods of high system traffic when the platform is scaling up.
- **Distribution variance:** If you send 30 requests per second over 2 seconds, the servers might receive 25 requests in the first second and 33 in the next (with 3 being limited), due to network conditions affecting request arrival rates.
- **Free tier ambiguity:** While third-party reviews note that no explicit numeric rate limit is published for the free tier (requiring developers to infer headroom from response headers), the official error code documentation specifies the 30 requests/second limit for handling `EXCEEDED_FREQ_LIMIT` errors ([the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/liveapi/guides/v4/api-error-codes.html)).

**Monitoring:** You can track usage via these HTTP response headers returned with every API call:
- `x-requests-remaining`: Usage credits remaining until quota reset
- `x-requests-used`: Usage credits used since last quota reset  
- `x-requests-last`: Usage cost of the last API call ([the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/liveapi/guides/v4/))

## Pricing Tiers (2026)

The Odds API uses a **credit-based subscription model** where cost depends on the number of markets and regions queried. Historical odds data costs 10x more credits than standard odds requests.

| Tier | Monthly Credits | Price (USD) | Notes |
|------|----------------|-------------|-------|
| **Starter (Free)** | 500 | $0 | Self-serve free plan including all sports, most bookmakers, all betting markets, and historical odds access |
| **Basic** | 20,000 | $30 | Entry-level paid tier |
| **Pro/Scale** | Up to 15,000,000 | $249 | High-volume tier |

*Pricing structure verified via [apibetting.com](https://www.apibetting.com/providers/the-odds-api) and [the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/liveapi/guides/v4/)*

**Credit Consumption Rates:**
- **Standard odds requests:** `cost = [number of markets] × [number of regions]` (1 credit per region per market)
- **Historical odds requests:** `cost = 10 × [number of markets] × [number of regions]` (10 credits per region per market)

## Important Technical Notes

1. **Historical Data Access:** While historical odds are technically available on the free Starter plan according to third-party reviews, the official V4 documentation states that the historical odds endpoint is "only available on paid usage plans" ([the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/liveapi/guides/v4/)). Historical snapshots are available from June 6, 2020 (10-minute intervals) and from September 2022 (5-minute intervals).

2. **Architecture:** The service is REST-only with polling; there is no WebSocket or streaming delivery, which may impact latency-sensitive in-play betting applications ([apibetting.com](https://www.apibetting.com/providers/the-odds-api)).

3. **429 Error Handling:** If rate limited, the documentation recommends spacing out requests over several seconds and avoiding unnecessary calls to static endpoints (like `/sports` or `/events`) that change infrequently ([the-odds-api.com](https://the-odds-api.com/liveapi/guides/v4/api-error-codes.html)).
